task_row_model.query: How can I implement a thread-safe in-memory LRU cache in Python that supports a TTL per entry and avoids race conditions when multiple threads insert or update the same key?

documents.content: In practice a simple LRU cache in Python can be built with collections.OrderedDict. The dict maps keys to stored values, and on each access the key is moved to the end with move_to_end(key) to mark it as most recently used. When inserting, set the key and then, if the number of entries exceeds the configured capacity, evict the least-recently-used item with popitem(last=False). One straightforward variant stores tuples as values, e.g., (value, expiry_timestamp), so that expiry can be checked at access time and expired entries treated as misses.
documents.reasoning_trace: Included OrderedDict methods and storing expiry tuples to support LRU movement and capacity eviction.

documents.content: Concurrent access introduces race conditions when two threads perform check-then-insert or update operations. The canonical remedy is to serialize modifications with a threading.Lock: acquire the lock around any operation that mutates the underlying OrderedDict or that calls move_to_end, since move_to_end is a mutating operation. A simple pattern is to hold the lock for get and put operations that touch ordering or insertion, preventing two threads from inserting the same key concurrently or inconsistently updating expiry values.
documents.reasoning_trace: Explained need to lock around mutations and ordering updates to prevent races during insert/update.

documents.content: For TTL support, store an expiry timestamp per entry computed via time.monotonic() + ttl_seconds to avoid clock-jump issues. On get, compare the stored expiry to time.monotonic(): if expired, delete the key and return a cache miss; otherwise update its LRU position and return its value. On put, set the new (value, expiry) tuple and move the key to the end. Optionally run a background daemon thread that periodically scans keys and removes expired entries to bound memory use, but lazy eviction on access is sufficient for correctness.
documents.reasoning_trace: Described using monotonic timestamps, lazy eviction on access, updating expiry on put, and optional background cleanup.

documents.content: Caching is a long-studied optimization technique dating back to early operating systems and CPU design. Reference texts often define cache hits, misses, and replacement policies; LRU is popular for its simplicity. Many tutorials include boilerplate code examples and historical notes tracing LRU usage in file system buffers. While such background is useful for pedagogy, implementation decisions for production code should emphasize concurrency and measurement over history and theoretical optimality claims.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Use collections.OrderedDict mapping key -> (value, expiry). On get: acquire a threading.Lock, check if key exists; if expiry <= time.monotonic() delete and return miss; otherwise move_to_end(key) and return value. On put: acquire the lock, set dict[key] = (value, time.monotonic()+ttl), move_to_end(key); if len>capacity evict with popitem(last=False). Optional: run a daemon thread to periodically remove expired entries.
